definitions.explanation: A secondary earthquake tremor that follows the main quake, swinging the ground back.
A return swing or counter-reaction following a major change or trend. Used figuratively for social, political, or economic reversals.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}の{後|あと}に{揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しがあった。
examples.english: There were aftershocks after the big earthquake.

examples.japanese: {揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しに{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
{余震|よしん}や{揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しに{備|そな}えて{避難|ひなん}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: We continued to take shelter in preparation for aftershocks and secondary tremors.

examples.japanese: {改革|かいかく}に{対|たい}する{揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しが{起|お}きた。
examples.english: A backlash against the reforms occurred.

examples.japanese: {株価|かぶか}の{急落|きゅうらく}の{後|あと}、{揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しで{少|すこ}し{回復|かいふく}した。
examples.english: After the sharp drop in stock prices, there was a slight recovery on the rebound.

examples.japanese: {急速|きゅうそく}な{変化|へんか}の{後|あと}には、{必|かなら}ず{揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しがくるものだ。
examples.english: After rapid changes, a swing back always comes.

notes:
Literally "swing back" from {揺|ゆ}る (to shake) + {戻|もど}す (to return). The physical image of a pendulum swinging back underlies both the seismological and figurative meanings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しが{来|く}る: a rebound/backlash comes
- {揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しが{起|お}きる: a rebound/backlash occurs
- {揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}しに{注意|ちゅうい}: beware of aftershocks / backlash

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {余震|よしん}: aftershock (seismological) — the standard technical term for earthquake aftershocks, while {揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}し is more descriptive and also extends to figurative use
- {反動|はんどう}: reaction, recoil — similar figurative meaning of counter-reaction, but emphasizes the force of opposition rather than the swinging-back motion
- リバウンド: rebound (loanword) — commonly used for weight regain after dieting, while {揺|ゆ}り{戻|もど}し covers broader social and political reversals
